headline: LinkedIn spent $5,417 in 14 days with zero conversions, so I paused it. Meta's CPA is up 50%, so I trimmed it. The direct-traffic surge looks AI-driven, not paid.

moves.reason: 0 conversions for 14 days on $5,417 spend; daily spend rose from ~$300 to $477 (above $450 budget) while conversions fell from ~1.5/day to 0 from 10/18. Self-reported LinkedIn share is 0% for two weeks, so it's not just a tracking break. Prior 4wk CPA was already $238, ROAS 0.77. Pause is cheap to reverse.

CPA stepped up from ~$60 to ~$91 since 9/28 (weekly CPA $111, $84, $80, $92, $93) at flat spend (~$3.5k/wk); ROAS 3.1 to 2.0. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from ~16% to ~10%, so the decline looks real. Models still credit meta 15-22%, so trim 20% rather than pause.

tests.hypothesis: Google's last-touch credit (69% share, CPA $18) overstates its incremental value; first-touch gives 40% (CPA $32). Part of the conversions it catches would happen anyway, e.g. from AI-assistant referrals who then search the brand.
tests.design: Geo holdout: pause brand-term search in ~20% of matched regions for 4 weeks and keep the rest as control. Measure total conversions (tracked + direct) per region, plus self-reported 'Google' share. Compare drops in total conversions with the drop in Google-reported conversions.

tests.hypothesis: Email is undervalued by last touch (4% share, CPA $20) vs first touch (23%, CPA $3.52) and Markov (17%). Spend is only ~$280/wk, so under-investment is cheap to test.
tests.design: Randomly hold out 20% of the subscriber list from campaigns for 4 weeks. Measure conversions per recipient in each group, plus the 'Your newsletter' self-reported share (currently ~9-13%).

flag_verdicts.reason: LinkedIn had 0 conversions on $5,417 over 14 days. Daily spend rose from ~$300 to $477, above its $450 budget. Self-reported LinkedIn share is 0% for two weeks. Paused.

Meta CPA moved from ~$60 to ~$91 (1.5x) at flat spend. ROAS fell from ~3.1 to 2.0. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from ~16% to ~10%. Trimmed budget 20%, not paused, because the models still credit it 15-22%.
The 9/12-9/18 Google spend spike (week of 9/14: $6,747) kept CPA at $20.82 vs $19.47 the week before. ROAS held at 9.2. Spend returned to ~$4.1k/wk with CPA falling to ~$15.6. No action.

Direct rose from 2.0 to 7.7/day while paid spend moved 1.04x. Self-reported 'Asked ChatGPT' plus 'AI assistant' rose from ~8% to ~22%. This points to untracked AI-referral discovery, not paid. No paid channel gets credit and no budget moves toward it. I can't buy this channel directly, so keep monitoring.

flags.message: linkedin spent $5,417 over 14 days with zero conversions, and spend is still rising.
meta CPA rose 1.5x, from $60 to $91, starting 2026-09-28.
google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA held at $22 vs $19. Likely fine, confirm before acting.
Direct conversions grew 3.9x (2.0 to 7.7/day) while paid spend moved 1.04x. Self-reported AI answers went from 8% to 22%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
